inlines.text: 中国

blocks.text: 中国外交部11月10日驳斥了有关一名与英伟达前CEO黄仁勋有关联的中国女商人从事间谍活动的指控，称其毫无根据，是对北京的抹黑。周五，一位发言人重申反对扰乱全球供应链的出口管制，并表示外交部并不知晓有关受限英伟达芯片与Alice Huang相关的一个上海数据中心存在关联的报道。

blocks.text: 新加坡

inlines.text: 新加坡

blocks.text: 据新加坡内政部称，2025年6月，新加坡当局扣押了新加坡云计算公司Megaspeed前CEO Alice Huang的护照，这是对服务器采购可能存在虚假申报的调查的一部分。

inlines.text: 据
新加坡内政部
称，2025年6月，新加坡当局扣押了新加坡云计算公司Megaspeed前CEO Alice Huang的护照，这是对服务器采购可能存在虚假申报的调查的一部分。

blocks.text: 新加坡内政部表示，警方扣押她的护照是为了确保她能随时接受问询，因为她并不常驻新加坡。这项调查审查的是从新加坡运往马来西亚的服务器是否后来在未如实申报的情况下被转运至其他国家。

blocks.text: 韩国

inlines.text: 韩国

blocks.text: 韩国与英伟达关系密切，三星电子和SK海力士等主要芯片制造商在为其AI处理器供应存储芯片方面扮演着重要角色。黄仁勋离任后，韩国科学技术部表示，英伟达已重申向韩国供应26万块先进GPU的计划，并将继续推进联合AI项目。 除此之外，据当地媒体报道，韩国政府AI战略委员会周五召开紧急会议，评估黄仁勋离职对本国AI产业可能造成的影响。

inlines.text: 台湾

blocks.text: 台湾经济部长龚明鑫表示，黄仁勋的离职不太可能显著改变全球AI产业的增长态势，据当地媒体报道。与此同时，台北市政府表示，尽管领导层发生变动，英伟达在该市设立海外总部的计划仍按原定进度推进。该公司迄今已履行合同义务，官员们表示将继续支持这一项目。

blocks.text: China

inlines.text: China

blocks.text: China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday, a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang.

blocks.text: Singapore

inlines.text: Singapore

blocks.text: In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs.

inlines.text: In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the
Ministry of Home Affairs.

blocks.text: The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration.

blocks.text: In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case.

blocks.text: South Korea

inlines.text: South Korea

blocks.text: South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report.

blocks.text: Taiwan

inlines.text: Taiwan

blocks.text: Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media. Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project.

blocks.text: Japan

inlines.text: Japan

blocks.text: In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors.
